dossier.summary: Tidewater Marine Fabrication builds aluminum hulls and deck structures for workboats at a yard in Wilmington, North Carolina. About 260 people, most of them welders and fitters. Welding runs on two shifts.
dossier.why_now: Listed four open welder positions on its careers page this month.

data.title: Pick your first automation cell in one day
data.tagline: A full day on the demo floor for fabricators. You bring drawings for the parts you weld most, score them for a robotic cell, and leave with one part picked, a layout sketch and a payback sheet.
data.audience: Operations and production leads at fabricators and job shops with 100 to 1,000 people.

agenda.title: What a cell does well, and what it does badly
agenda.note: Seam types, part sizes and fixturing, from cells we have put on shop floors.

agenda.title: Score your parts
agenda.note: Run each drawing you brought through the scorecard: seam length, repeat volume, fixturing, rework.

agenda.title: Weld it on the demo cell
agenda.note: We program your top-scoring part on the cell and run it, so you see a cycle time instead of hearing a claim.

agenda.title: Sketch the layout
agenda.note: Where the cell sits in your shop, what feeds it, and who runs it. On paper, on our floor plan grid.

agenda.title: Fill in the payback sheet
agenda.note: Hours by part from your own numbers, cell cost, and the staffing you have today. The sheet is yours to keep.

agenda.title: Read-outs
agenda.note: Each team shows its part, layout and sheet. We send the photos and the cell program after.

bring: Drawings for the two or three parts you weld the most
Last quarter's hours by part, if you track them
Steel-toe boots and safety glasses for the floor
The person who would run the cell day to day
data.host_note: Idris Okonkwo programs the demo cell and runs the day with two applications engineers. Eight people, so every team gets time on the cell.
data.confirm_note: Your seat is confirmed by email within a day, with directions to the floor and the scorecard to fill in beforehand.
data.why_now: Listed four open welder positions on its careers page this month.
data.why_you: Tidewater runs welding on two shifts and has four welder positions open this month. The day is built around that gap: which hull or deck parts a cell could take off your welders first, scored from your own drawings.

leave_with.lead: One hull or deck part picked for a cell
leave_with.text: Scored from the drawings you bring, by seam length, repeat volume and fixturing, then run on the demo cell so you leave with a measured cycle time.

leave_with.lead: A layout sketch for the Wilmington yard
leave_with.text: Where the cell sits, how aluminum sections reach it across two shifts, and who on each shift runs it.

leave_with.lead: A payback sheet using your own hours
leave_with.text: Hours by part from your records against the cell cost and the four welder openings, ready to take to whoever signs off.
